title: Can You Build an App with Just a ChatGPT Plus Subscription?

body_markdown:
Yes for writing the app, partly for running it. ChatGPT Plus ($20 a month) gives you an AI that writes code, and its Sites beta hosts simple apps. If your app is a simple shared tool, Plus can be enough. If it takes payments or needs its own email logins, you need hosting and services from somewhere else.


## The short version


ChatGPT Plus costs $20 a month and covers the thinking: writing, fixing, and explaining code.


Plus includes Codex, a coding agent, with a 5-hour usage cap again since August 25, 2026.


ChatGPT Sites, a public beta on Plus, hosts simple apps with a small database, and it does not allow payments.


On other routes, the host, database, logins, and domain are separate accounts.


On Floot, ChatGPT does the thinking and Floot builds and hosts the whole app, with no second AI bill.


The rest of this guide covers what Plus gives you, what it leaves out, how to tell if it is enough, and what each route makes you do.


## Plus and your app, in one picture


Think of a building. ChatGPT Plus is the architect: it draws every plan and fixes the drawings when something is wrong.


An architect does not give you the building. Someone still pours the foundation (hosting), builds the filing room (the database), staffs the front desk (logins), and puts an address on the door (the domain).


The split exists because writing an app and running it are different jobs.


## What Plus actually gives you


Plus gives you four things for building, as of Sept 25, 2026.


It **writes the code** . Describe a feature or paste an error, and it answers in the chat.


It **works on a whole project** . Codex is an agent that edits every file in a code project. (An agent is an AI that takes several steps on its own.)


It **hosts simple apps** . Sites turns a chat into a web app with a link, a database of up to 10 GB, file storage, and "Sign in with ChatGPT."


It **connects to outside tools** . Connectors let ChatGPT hand work to other services, which is how an app builder plugs in.


Notice the pattern. Everything Plus does well happens inside the chat, and a live app lives outside it.


## What Plus covers and what it does not


Plus fully covers the code and only partly covers running it.


AI that writes the code. Covered by Plus: Yes.


Coding agent (Codex). Covered by Plus: Yes, with a 5-hour cap and a weekly cap.


Hosting. Covered by Plus: Partly: Sites beta, with beta usage limits.


Database. Covered by Plus: Partly: Sites, up to 10 GB.


Logins. Covered by Plus: Partly: "Sign in with ChatGPT" only.


Payments. Covered by Plus: No, Sites does not allow them.


Custom domain. Covered by Plus: Partly: Sites connects one you already own.


A tutoring booking app needs email logins, a bookings table, Stripe checkout, and confirmation emails. Plus writes all of it, and most of it runs elsewhere.


## Is Plus enough for your app?


Ask whether your app takes money or needs people to make their own accounts.


If neither, Plus and Sites can be enough. A team poll, an internal tracker, and a quiz all fit.


If either, you need more than Plus. That covers a store, a paid booking app, and a client portal with email logins. (Sites also launched without the EEA, the UK, or Switzerland.)


## What each route makes you do


Every route uses Plus for the code. They differ in who runs the app.


Copy and paste means you move ChatGPT's files into a project and deploy them to a host like Vercel. Every error means another round of copying.


Codex with GitHub means Codex pushes changes and a host deploys them. You add a database and a login service as you grow, so you manage three or four accounts.


Sites stops at payments and your own logins.


The pattern is the same everywhere it goes wrong: the code is finished, then the first real user sends you off to set up a host, a database, and a login service, one account at a time.


Floot is the part Plus does not buy you, and it runs inside ChatGPT. You describe the app in ChatGPT, your Plus plan pays for the thinking, and your assistant builds it onto Floot: pages, small server programs called endpoints ("save my order," "send the confirmation"), and a Postgres database, live on its own URL from the first build.


Because Floot also includes the database, logins with Google, Microsoft, and email, file storage, email sending, scheduled jobs, and live updates, along with Stripe for payments, every missing line in the table above is already there. You never sign up for anything else, and there is no second AI bill. Floot meters its own building actions, which reset daily: Free 100 a day, Pro $25 a month for 1,000, Power $100 a month for 5,000. Your ChatGPT usage cap still applies to the thinking.


## FAQ


## Can I build an app with ChatGPT Plus?


Yes. Plus writes the code and Sites hosts simple apps, but apps with payments or email logins need services from elsewhere.


## Is ChatGPT Plus enough to build an app?


It is enough to write one, and to run one only if Sites can handle it.


## Does ChatGPT Plus include hosting?


Partly. The Sites beta hosts simple web apps on Plus, with beta usage limits and no payments.


## Can I build an app with ChatGPT without coding?


Yes, through Sites for simple apps, or by connecting an app builder like Floot inside ChatGPT.


## What are the ChatGPT Plus limits for coding?


A rolling 5-hour cap, back since August 25, 2026, plus a weekly quota. Pro removes the 5-hour cap.


## Does Floot work with ChatGPT Plus?


Yes. ChatGPT does the thinking on your Plus plan, and Floot builds and hosts the app with the database, logins, and payments included.
